method: Compared all 11 hash-checked candidate crops with rendered original slides 2, 3, 5, 7, 8 and 9. Dispositions are proposed local content judgments, not saved product review decisions or independent Gold approval.

objects.evidenceText: The abstract contrasts a legacy vehicle with several domain ECUs connected by different buses against an SDV paradigm with a central ECU and Ethernet links; the drawing is schematic.
objects.reason: Both vehicle schematics and their A/B labels are visible on the original slide; the graphic does not specify a measured topology benefit.

objects.evidenceText: The slide legend identifies LIN, CAN, Ethernet and FlexRay link colors, plus sensor triangles and actuator circles.
objects.reason: The legend is legible in the crop and original slide; it describes this schematic only.

objects.evidenceText: The presentation juxtaposes an Ethernet II header with destination/source MAC fields and EtherType against an IEEE 802.11 header with Address 1 (RA), Address 2 (TA), Address 3 and Address 4; the shown example has MAC A/MAC B, BSSID and N/A in the 802.11 positions.
objects.reason: Labels and mapping lines are visible on original slide 3. The diagram is an example of the authors' forwarding discussion, not a complete general header translation rule.

objects.evidenceText: The slide illustrates encapsulation: an original Ethernet packet with HOST_2/HOST_1 and 0x8000 is forwarded toward the wireless interface with an added outer RSU/OBU Ethernet header marked 0x08AF.
objects.reason: The original and forwarded packet rows and their relationship are visible on slide 5; this records the proposed SD4ADDR format, not a standard mandate.

objects.evidenceText: The slide illustrates decapsulation: the received packet has outer RSU/OBU and 0x08AF ahead of HOST_2/HOST_1 and 0x8000, while the forwarded packet retains the inner HOST_2/HOST_1 and 0x8000 header after removing the outer header.
objects.reason: The received and forwarded packet rows are legible on original slide 5.

objects.evidenceText: The authors' Ethernet-interface forwarding-time chart labels normal 4.639 μs, encap 4.990 μs and decap 5.943 μs; the slide attributes the higher decap time to recirculation and reparsing of the decapsulated packet.
objects.reason: All three bar labels, unit and explanatory bullet are legible on original slide 7; the OCR misreads some chart text and is not the source of this transcription.
Photograph illustrates the Ethernet test setup. Visible connector counts and device stickers do not establish an equipment model or performance result and are not needed to support the chart values.
Photograph illustrates wireless test equipment below the charts; its NAP stickers and ports do not establish measured throughput or a product specification.

objects.evidenceText: The authors' IEEE 802.11p throughput chart compares Default versus SD4ADDR by Layer 4 payload bytes: 20: 0.43/0.43; 50: 1.04/1.04; 100: 2.00/2.00; 200: 3.78/3.71; 500: 7.81/7.69; 1000: 12.03/11.88; 1472: 14.69/14.54 Mbps.
objects.reason: Axes, legend and paired labels are legible in crop and original slide 8. Values are presentation test results, not a general product or standard performance claim.

objects.evidenceText: The authors' Ethernet target-throughput chart shows matching Default and SD4ADDR values at 10, 20, 50, 100, 200 and 400 Mbps target settings; each bar pair is labeled with the target value in Mbps.
objects.reason: Axes, legend and all six paired bar labels are legible in crop and original slide 8. This supports the tested settings shown, not unlimited throughput equivalence.

Aveiro map contains colored pin, house, point and route marks but no complete legend identifying their types or timestamps. Slide body says 22 RSUs were active as of July 2025; that number is separate native text and cannot safely be mapped onto the plotted symbols or claimed current.

next: Keep the unlabeled deployment map unresolved. Resolve source use and map provenance before attempting full-document product review completion; then verify user-visible citations and question independence prior to Gold freeze.
